summary: Fund-transfer failures are caused by an expired client mTLS certificate on payment-service (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z). From 12:15:27Z every call to bank-partner-api is rejected (TLS alert 45), so payments are set to PENDING_RETRY rather than returned as HTTP 5xx. That is why the HTTP error-rate panel stays ~0.2% (green) while the real signals diverge sharply: bank_api_error_rate rose to 100% and payment_success_rate collapsed to ~2.5%. The metric that would have caught this (bank_api_error_rate / payment_success_rate) simply wasn't the one on the dashboard. No payment-service deployment occurred and the only config change (timeout 3000->5000 at 11:20) predates onset and is unrelated; request_rate and CPU were flat and latency fell, ruling out load/saturation. This is credential_expiry, matching historical incident HIST-106 (same failure mode, no renewal automation).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired payment-service client mTLS certificate breaks bank-partner-api calls
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal used by payment-service for mTLS to bank-partner-api expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z. bank-partner-api rejects the handshake (TLS alert 45), so all outbound payment/fund-transfer calls fail and are marked PENDING_RETRY. Because these are not surfaced as HTTP 5xx, the HTTP error_rate panel stays green while bank_api_error_rate hits 100% and payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%.

causal_chain.claim: cert expiry -> mTLS handshake rejected by bank-partner-api (alert 45)
handshake failure -> payments marked PENDING_RETRY, not 5xx
no 5xx -> HTTP error_rate flat while bank_api_error_rate=100% and success_rate~2.5%

assumptions: The 'our client cert' referenced is the credential payment-service presents to bank-partner-api.
bank-partner-api enforces mTLS and rejects the expired client cert (consistent with alert 45 in logs).

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner API outage (dependency failure)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: bank-partner-api is degraded/unavailable (as in HIST-105), causing payment failures independent of our certificate.
assumptions: Logs would show 5xx/timeout rather than an explicit cert-expiry error.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Logs explicitly show a TLS 'expired certificate (alert 45)' error naming OUR client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, not partner-side 5xx/timeouts; endpoint is our credential failure.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change (bank.api.timeout_ms raise) caused failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Raising bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 11:20 caused payment failures.
assumptions: A timeout change could somehow produce an explicit cert-expiry error.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Change predates onset by ~55 min; latency did not increase (dropped), and error cause is an explicit cert expiry, unrelated to timeout value.

facts.statement: payment-service began logging mTLS handshake rejections to bank-partner-api at 12:15:27Z, with the client cert expired at 12:15:00Z.
bank_api_error_rate went to 100% and payment_success_rate fell to ~2.5% while HTTP error_rate stayed ~0.2%.
Failures are recorded as PENDING_RETRY, not HTTP 5xx, hiding them from the error-rate panel.
No payment-service deployment occurred; only a settlement-service deploy and an unrelated 11:20 timeout config change.
Traffic and resource metrics were normal/improving, ruling out load or saturation.
A prior near-identical incident (HIST-106) was an expired client certificate with no renewal automation.

assumptions: The 'our client cert' in the log is the credential payment-service presents to bank-partner-api.
bank-partner-api enforces mTLS and rejects the expired cert (consistent with alert 45).
bank-partner-api has no telemetry (has_telemetry=false), so its side could not be directly queried.

timeline.event: payment-service client mTLS cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires (notAfter).
First payment marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected.
First explicit 'tls: expired certificate (alert 45)' log; 171 such errors accumulate.
bank_api_error_rate begins climbing (62.58 avg) toward 100%; payment_success_rate starts dropping.
Incident reported by support (reported service payment-service).
bank_api_error_rate still 100%, payment_success_rate still ~2.2%; incident ongoing.

recommended_actions.action: Rotate/renew the payment-service client certificate for bank-partner-api and force an immediate reload/restart of the mTLS client so handshakes succeed.
recommended_actions.rationale: The expired cert (notAfter 12:15:00Z) is the direct cause; renewal restores bank-partner-api calls.

recommended_actions.action: After renewal, replay/clear the PENDING_RETRY backlog of stranded fund transfers.
recommended_actions.rationale: 40+ customer transfers are stuck in PENDING_RETRY and not yet completed.

recommended_actions.action: Add certificate-expiry alerting (e.g. <14 days to notAfter) and renewal automation, as was done after HIST-106.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-106 was the same failure mode; no renewal automation/expiry alert exists.

recommended_actions.action: Fix dashboards/alerting to surface bank_api_error_rate and payment_success_rate (business-level signals), not just HTTP 5xx error_rate.
recommended_actions.rationale: PENDING_RETRY failures bypass the HTTP 5xx panel, giving a false-green dashboard.

data_gaps: bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry=false, so its own status/errors could not be independently confirmed (mitigated by explicit client-side cert-expiry error).
No direct metric for the specific client certificate's validity/expiry was available; expiry is inferred from the explicit log line.
PENDING_RETRY backlog size and whether retries eventually succeed after renewal were not measurable from available data.

findings.statement: The client certificate used by payment-service to call bank-partner-api expired at 2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, causing TLS alert 45 (certificate expired).
payment-service bank_api_error_rate jumped from ~0.2% to 100% in the 12:12-12:20 buckets and stayed 100% through 13:56.
payment-service payment_success_rate collapsed from ~99% to ~2-3% in the 12:12-12:20 buckets and remained ~2-3% through 13:56.
payment-service HTTP error_rate remained flat ~0.2% across the entire window (11:00-13:56), explaining the green dashboard.
Failed payments are recorded as PENDING_RETRY rather than surfaced as HTTP 5xx, so the HTTP error-rate panel does not reflect them.

findings.statement: payment-service request_rate was stable ~100 req/s and latency_p99 DROPPED from ~320ms to ~140ms at onset (no load or saturation spike).
The only config change in window was payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z, ~55 min before onset.
The only deployment in window was settlement-service v1.9.0 (CSV exporter) at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z; no payment-service deployment occurred.
A prior incident HIST-106 (settlement-service, 2025-06-30) had the same pattern: client certificate expired, no renewal automation.
